crime_highlights: The theft of the motor vehicle, the dangerous driving of it, and the striking of the police car, resulting in Constable Morrison being injured are very concerning.
you, at age 12, at the behest of two older youth became involved in this caper that went badly wrong
Any one of you involved in this could have been injured or killed.
rationale_highlights: You, yourself, even at age 13, have experienced a number of these challenges, poverty, housing instability, child welfare involvement, lack of success in school, addictions in your family, family breakdown and violence.
So even though those things happened long before you were born, they are still present in your community, in your family and in your life.
I must consider and give true consideration to your circumstances as a Mi’kmaq young person
I am satisfied that the sentence that is appropriate for you is one that is less than 18 months
note: Youth; conclusion in para 17 is general, not explicit culpability reduction.

crime_highlights: Mr. Syliboy walked into the Shopper’s Drug Mart at 5524 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, Nova Scotia, and asked the pharmacist for a pen and paper
With those, he wrote a note saying: he wanted hydromorphone, robbery, he didn’t want violence.
He got the drugs and walked out of the store, not rushing.
Mr. Syliboy wanted to be arrested so he would be held at the Burnside Correctional Facility, where his father was on remand.
the victim noted her concern for the potential for violence
rationale_highlights: Mr. Syliboy has experienced the adverse impact of many factors continuing to plaque Aboriginal communities post-colonization
his moral culpability is reduced given his distrust and alienation from this system, resultant from his experiences as an Indigenous person and the colonial history of the system itself
Again, his moral culpability is reduced considering his life circumstances as an Indigenous person.
These are direct reflections of the impact of colonialism and racism on Indigenous communities.

crime_highlights: Mr. Lafitte was searched incidental to his arrest and in the front pockets of his sweatpants, police officers located $765 in Canadian currency
police officers seized three ziploc bags containing a total of 16.2 grams (including the weight of the bag) of cannabis marijuana
a plastic “baggie” containing, according to the Health Canada analyst, 44 pink-colored 6 mg hydromorphone pills
a “baggie” with a white substance which Health Canada confirmed to be 5.7 grams (out of bag weight) of crack cocaine
rationale_highlights: Mr. Lafitte has personally experienced the adverse impact of many factors which continue to plague aboriginal communities across Canada
I have considered the number of Gladue factors that Mr. Lafitte has personally experienced and undoubtedly been affected by them
I have taken those factors into account
note: Drug case; Gladue only modestly affected sentence; no violence or victim harm.
